Meadow: Open turf with grouped alder, oak and fruit trees, brushy edges and grassy glades that follow the same neighborhood pattern.
BirchGrove: Light birch-dominated groves of mixed heights, separated by grassy glades and brushy margins with litter and flowers.
DenseForest: Closed oak stands alternate with open glades and brushy edges; moss, ferns, leaf litter and fungi follow the canopy.
FlowerMeadow: Rich wildflower colonies and occasional flowering shrubs alternate with short-grass openings; hives occupy the richer patches.
Orchard: Fruit-tree groves of varied ages alternate with grassy clearings; fallen fruit stays close to actual fruit trees.
PineHighlands: Upland pines and spruces form uneven stands around open glades, over podzol, ferns, lichen and scattered stone groups.
SnowyTundra: Open tundra where snow lingers in colder sheltered patches and thins to frozen turf, with sparse low plants and lichen.
SnowyPeaks: Cold alpine heights with lingering snow, warmer patches of native rock and exposed cliffs beneath the summit.
FrozenLake: Cold lowland water sealed by clear and black ice.
TaigaBog: Small spruce and pine stands over snowy peat, with cotton-grass colonies and lichen margins.
Desert: Pale dune desert with broad young barrel cacti, slender juveniles and mature plants bearing unequal arms and tapered crowns.
RedDesert: Iron-red sand with varied cactus silhouettes, sparse thorny growth and localized red-rock groups separated by open ground.
Savanna: Open acacia canopies of varied heights above broad tall-grass colonies and dry scrub.
Badlands: Eroded mesa country with visible clay strata.
Steppe: Dry grass and gravel plains with low grass colonies, scrub margins and wide open gaps.
Marsh: Willows and alder above muddy shallows, with dense reed colonies and sedge margins.
MangroveCoast: Tidal mud coast held by mangrove roots.
Rainforest: Jungle, fig and palm stands alternate with brushy gaps; shaded ferns and bromeliads follow the canopy, while vines cling to real trunks.
RiverDelta: Low clay-and-gravel river mouths with reed beds grading into sedge at their edges.
GravelShore: Gravel and cobble coast with stranded timber along real shorelines.
OceanFloor: Submerged gravel and clay with scattered kelp colonies and seagrass at their margins.
CoralShallows: Shallow reef with color-coherent coral colonies, varying heights and seagrass margins.
RockyHighlands: Exposed gravel and cobble uplands with shouldered boulders, scattered conifers and colonies of mountain flowers and lichen.
Volcanic: Basaltic ash and lava rock with obsidian, magma and sculpted fumarole-like mineral formations.
HotSprings: Descending mineral terrace fans hold shallow pools beside dry sinter bridges and low, uneven mineral cups with recessed mouths.
BambooThicket: Dense jointed bamboo with tender shoots.
CherryGrove: Cherry woodland with petal carpets concentrated around trees.
AutumnForest: Amber and russet groves alternate with grassy glades; litter, fallen timber and fungi collect beneath the canopy.
Heathland: Purple heather colonies separated by short grass and open rock.
LavenderFields: Broad lavender colonies across rich rolling turf, separated by low grassy margins.
RollingDowns: Broad chalky ridges and hollows carry cropped grass, flint, grouped low growth and open grassy clearings.
WetlandFen: Sedge-dominated peat wetland, with cotton grass at the colony margins and open water between stands.
OldGrowthForest: Broad veteran crowns rise above younger trees and brushy edges, with open glades, fern-rich shade and fungi beside fallen timber.
IceSpikes: Cold field of tall wind-carved ice spires.
FrozenFjord: Snowy glacial inlet above dark deep water and slate scree.
AuroraTundra: Open permafrost with faintly luminous lichen; lingering snow breaks into frozen-turf patches along warmer margins.
FirnField: High compacted-snow field split by blue crevasses.
BorealBurn: Charred fallen logs among pine, birch and spruce, with bright fireweed colonies and grassy gaps.
Oasis: Mixed-height palms around fresh water, with dates near their trunks and grass grading into reeds.
SaltFlats: Open salt pans with crust seams and subtle surface patterns; shrubs and stone groups remain absent.
DuneSea: Broad dunes with asymmetric crests, sandstone fragments and extensive open sand.
Scrubland: Low mesquite trees and loose thorn-bush colonies separated by dry-scrub margins.
PaintedHills: Eroded hills of ochre, umber, and sienna clay.
KarstPinnacles: Jagged limestone towers draped in hanging vines.
CloudForest: Shortened fig-dominated groves and brushy edges occupy humid highlands, with moss near roots and ferns fringed by bromeliads.
PeatBog: Cotton-grass-dominated colonies over saturated peat and bog iron, with sedge at their margins.
BlackwaterBayou: Tall cypress and willow over dark water, with knees beside cypress roots and lilies in shallow pools.
FloodedGrassland: Seasonally flooded mud plain with tall reeds and lilies.
TepuiPlateau: Rain-darkened high plateau carrying bromeliads and endemic flowers.
BlackSandBeach: Basaltic coast covered by black volcanic sand.
ShellBeach: Pale coast of shell sand and driftwood.
TidePools: Low rocky coast rich in anemones, starfish, and barnacles.
SeaStacks: Layered sandstone coast with pale guano patches and low, weathered rock groups.
DeepKelpForest: Tall underwater kelp colonies rooted on the seabed, with lower seagrass fringes and open-water gaps.
MeteorField: Scorched impact country with fused glass and iron fragments.
GeyserBasin: Geyserite terraces and sulfur-crusted pools dotted with sculpted mineral vents. The vents are static formations, without simulated eruptions.
LavaTubes: Ropy cooled lava above shallow basalt tubes.
GraniteDomes: Exfoliating granite uplands with overlapping stone plates, sparse pine stands and open rocky glades.
SlateQuarryHills: Layered slate hills carry angular scree fans, raised fragments and short stepped outcrops.
AmethystGorge: Dark gorge walls carry crystal clusters with unequal violet towers rising from low, connected beds of host rock.
MediterraneanWoodland: Compact oak, mesquite and fig among dry-shrub colonies, flowered margins and rocky clearings.
Chaparral: Dry scrub hills and shallow hollows hold grouped flat-crowned trees, low bushes, heather and sculpted boulder patches.
TemperateRainforest: Moist redwood, alder and giant-tree stands alternate with open glades, mossy roots, ferns, fallen timber and fungi.
RedwoodForest: Tall redwoods stand above younger trees and broadleaf groves, with open glades, fern-rich shade and fungi near fallen timber.
TallgrassPrairie: Dense, broad tall-grass colonies over rich soil, with wildflower margins and few trees.
Pampas: Open grassland with pale plume-grass colonies and low green margins.
MonsoonForest: Jungle, fig and palm stands over muddy ground open into grassy glades, with trunk-climbing vines and fern-rich margins.
TropicalDryForest: Shorter acacia, fig and eucalyptus groves alternate with dry grassy glades, leaf litter and brushy edges.
MiomboWoodland: Warm acacia, mesquite and fig groves alternate with broad grassy openings and dry, brushy margins.
AlpineMeadow: Colonies of mountain and endemic flowers on high turf above the main tree line, with lingering snow on colder ordinary ground.
PolarDesert: Extremely dry, wind-scoured polar gravel and frozen ground.
Muskeg: Sparse, stunted spruce and pine over waterlogged peat, with sedge colonies and cotton-grass margins.
FloodplainForest: Willow-dominated river woodland with alder and cypress, fern patches and reed-fringed wet ground.
InlandDelta: Landlocked mud-and-shallow-water mosaic with broad colonies of tall reeds and sedge margins.
Atoll: Low coral cay with shell sand, palms, sparse pale limestone stones on dry ground and shallow reef water.
CoastalDunes: Sheltered dune-grass tufts on pale coastal sand, with timber along real strandlines.
LimestonePavement: Exposed jointed limestone with thin turf-filled fissures.
GlacialMoraine: Unsorted boulders, gravel, and till left at a glacier margin.
GlacialOutwash: Flat sand-and-gravel plain deposited by glacial meltwater.
VolcanicCaldera: Broad basaltic crater rim surrounding an ash-covered basin.
ColdRiver: Cold clear water over gravel, with sparse reed-and-sedge margins.
TropicalRiver: Warm muddy river channels with denser reed fringes and fern-covered banks.
OpenOcean: Deep water beyond the continental shelf, with sparse surface life.
SeagrassLagoon: Shallow sandy lagoon with dense seagrass beds and open sand gaps.
AustralianBushland: Open eucalyptus woodland with dry-shrub colonies and low grassy margins.
AfricanThornveld: Scattered acacia above tight thorn-bush colonies and dry-scrub margins.
MontaneForest: Shorter spruce, pine and birch stands form a belt below alpine ground, with open glades, ferns and lichen margins.
TemperateSaltMarsh: Sedge and reed colonies around tidal shallows, with open deeper channels.
ChalkHeath: Open chalk country carrying purple heath and scattered flint.
RedRockSteppe: Dry continental grassland over rust-red ironstone outcrops.
MossyHighlands: Short pine and spruce groves rise from mossy cobble, with brushy edges, open glades, ferns and lichen.
